en: Theravāda Vinaya Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga Pācittiyakaṇḍa
The Chapter on the Naked (Naggavagga), Chapter 27: The Training Rule on Warding Off.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, a robe for the rainy season (*akālacīvara*) had arisen for the community of bhikkhunīs.
Then the community of bhikkhunīs gathered, desiring to divide that robe.
At that time, the bhikkhunīs who were the female pupils (*antevāsiniyo*) of the bhikkhunī Thullanandā had departed.
The bhikkhunī Thullanandā said this to those bhikkhunīs:
"Venerable ladies, the bhikkhunīs have departed; the robe-cloth will not yet be distributed.
She thus obstructed the distribution of the robe-cloth.
The bhikkhunīs departed, thinking, "The robe-cloth will not yet be distributed.
When the resident bhikkhunīs had arrived, the bhikkhunī Thullanandā had that robe-cloth distributed.
Those bhikkhunīs who were of few desires... [as above] ...were indignant, complained, and spread it about, saying:
“How can the noble lady Thullanandā obstruct a legitimate distribution of robe-cloth? … [The Buddha asked:
“Is it true, monks, that the bhikkhunī Thullanandā obstructs a legitimate distribution of robe-cloth?
“It is true, Blessed One.”
The Buddha, the Blessed One, rebuked them:
“… How can the bhikkhunī Thullanandā obstruct a legitimate distribution of robe-cloth?
This, bhikkhus, is neither for the inspiration of those without faith nor for the increase of those with faith…” [and so on].
And furthermore, monks, the nuns should recite this training rule as follows:
“Whichever nun should obstruct a legitimate distribution of robes, there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
Whichever nun:
Whichever [nun] of such a kind... "a nun" ...pe...
this is the nun intended in this context.
The distribution of robes known as the *dhammika* robe-distribution:
the united Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, having assembled, distributes them.
"Should she prevent" means...
If she objects, thinking, "How can this robe-cloth not be distributed?", there is an offense of expiation (pācittiya).
If it is legitimate and she perceives it as legitimate, yet she objects, there is an offense of expiation.
If it is legitimate and she is uncertain of its legitimacy, yet she objects, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one perceives what is lawful as unlawful, there is no offense.
If one perceives what is unlawful as lawful, there is an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
If one is in doubt regarding what is unlawful, there is an offense of wrong-doing.
If it is contrary to the Dhamma, but he perceives it as contrary to the Dhamma,
there is no offense.
There is no offense if he prevents [the action] by pointing out the benefit.
"Of one who is insane,
of one who is a first-offender.
The seventh training rule is concluded.
